meta.title: Character Stats · TBD MMO design wiki
meta.description: The six primary attributes, the derived combat stats they feed, resources, and how modifiers are applied.

intro.crumbs: Design wiki / 04 Systems / Character Stats
intro.lede: The agreed stat vocabulary. Exact values, scaling formulas, damage formulas and balance caps are still open.
intro.p: Players, NPCs and monsters share the same stat model. What separates them is their definition and the capabilities they have, not a different set of stats.

primary.title: Primary attributes

r2.c2: Accuracy, evasion, attack speed, physical critical chance

r3.c2: Max health, health regeneration, part of physical defense

r5.c2: Max mana, mana regeneration, magical defense, cast speed, magical critical chance

primary.p1: Primary attributes are inputs to the derived stats. They are not current resources, and they don’t directly represent an attack result.
primary.p2: Rule: movement speed should not scale strongly or directly from DEX. Otherwise DEX would improve accuracy, evasion, attack frequency, critical chance and mobility all at once, and become a mandatory attribute.

derived.title: Derived stats
derived.p1: Physical and magical attack are inputs to damage calculation, not final damage values. Attack speed shortens the basic-attack cycle, cast speed shortens ability preparation and casting time, and cooldown reduction shortens the reuse delay after an action completes. These are three separate mechanics.
derived.p2: Elemental resistance is keyed by damage type rather than a fixed field for every possible element. The supported damage types are not decided yet. Resistance may be negative.
derived.p3: Acceleration and deceleration belong to movement itself and are not part of the general stat set.
derived.p4: Current health and current mana are the character’s live resources, not derived stats.

order.title: How modifiers apply
order.p1: Values are resolved in a fixed order:
order.pre1:
base values of the character’s definition
+ permanent character modifiers
+ equipment modifiers
+ temporary effects
→ resolved attributes and stats
order.p2: Each stat follows the same pipeline:
order.pre2:
(base + flat modifiers)
× (1 + sum of additive percentages)
× final multipliers
→ clamp for that stat
order.p3: Every modifier carries a stable source, so everything an item, effect or progression node contributes can be replaced or removed together.
